city.Athens.description: In ancient times, Athens was a powerful city-state that warred with its neighbor Sparta and made lasting contributions to philosophy, science, drama and art.
city.Athens.flag: blue and white stripes with a white cross in the corner
city.Baghdad.description: Baghdad, with a population of about 8 million, is Iraq's capital and largest city.
city.Baghdad.flag: red, white and black bands with green Arabic script
city.Bamako.description: Bamako, with a population of around 3 million, is by far the largest city in Mali, an arid country located in West Africa and extending into the Sahara Desert.
city.Bamako.flag: three bands of green, yellow and red
city.Bangkok.description: Bangkok, the capital of Thailand, is a bustling city laced with canals and dotted with temples called wats.
city.Bangkok.flag: red, white and blue bands, the blue one twice as thick
city.Budapest.description: Hungary, with an area slightly smaller than Indiana, is bordered by Slovakia, Austria, Slovenia, Croatia, Serbia, Romania and Ukraine.
city.Budapest.greeting: In Hungarian, a friendly hi is “Szia” (SEE-yah).
city.Budapest.flag: three bands of red, white and green
city.Buenos Aires.description: Argentina is South America's second-largest nation, after Brazil. Its terrain ranges from tropical forests in the north to cold and barren Tierra del Fuego in the south.
city.Buenos Aires.flag: light blue and white bands with a golden sun
city.Cairo.description: Cairo, located at the mouth of the Nile River, is the largest city in Africa.
city.Cairo.flag: red, white and black bands with a golden eagle
city.Colombo.description: Sri Lanka has a hot, humid climate. The principal crops grown on this island nation are tea, coconuts and rice.
